p.scope-of-this-document: **Scope of this document.** How to write spec units that stay addressable and stay true: what a unit is, how normativity is marked, why norm and rationale live apart, how deviations are recorded, the size budgets, when to split a document, changelog lines, and the anchor-stability contract.

p.protocol-document-pointer: The addressing scheme itself is defined in [`ADDRESSABLE-SPECS-PROTOCOL.xml`](ADDRESSABLE-SPECS-PROTOCOL.xml).

p.A-SPEC-UNIT-IS-A-HEADING-SPAN: A **spec unit** is the span from an anchored heading to the next heading of the same or higher level.

p.AND-ALSO-MEANS-TWO-UNITS: If a unit needs "and also", it is two units.

p.A-UNIT-MUST-MAKE-SENSE-ALONE: The unit is the page of the agent's working memory: it must make sense *alone* when pulled into a context window without its neighbours.

p.a-context-dependent-unit-is-not-addressa: A unit that only works when the reader has just read the three sections above it is not addressable — its anchor points at a fragment, not a thought.

p.SOFT-CEILING-ONE-PAGE-PER-UNIT: Soft ceiling: a unit fits on a page, roughly 120 lines.

p.longer-units-page-badly: Longer units page badly and churn on every edit.

p.A-FENCE-CARRIES-NO-ANCHOR-AND-THAT-IS-DE: **Content inside a fenced block carries no anchor, and cannot be given one.** A fence is a payload — the reader copies it out, pastes it somewhere, runs it — so an anchor written inside would travel with the copy and corrupt what it is a copy of. Directives inside a fence are ignored for exactly the reason headings inside one are.

p.AN-INSTRUCTION-INSIDE-A-FENCE-IS-UNVERIF: The consequence is the part authors underestimate: **a fence carrying an INSTRUCTION rather than an illustration is unverified by construction.** No instrument can test its claim, none can register that a fix landed, and whether any of it is ever checked depends on which nearby anchor a reader happens to pick up. And these are exactly the lines most likely to be *run*: quick-start blocks, copy-paste prompts, worked commands.

p.A-CHECKABLE-CLAIM-BELONGS-OUTSIDE-THE-FE: So put every checkable claim **outside** the fence, in an anchored sentence next to it, and keep inside only what must be copied verbatim. A path, a version, a command name asserted inside a fence is a fact with no address and no reader — assert it in the prose that introduces the block, where it can be judged, and let the block demonstrate it.

p.A-READER-MUST-NEVER-GUESS-WHETHER-A-SENT: A reader — human or model — must never guess whether a sentence binds.

p.CONTRACT-STATEMENTS-USE-RFC-2119-VERBS: Contract statements use RFC-2119 verbs (MUST / SHOULD / MAY); everything without such a verb is explanation, not obligation.

td.ROW-KIND-DECISION-BINDS: the choice binds; the rationale does not

td.ROW-KIND-DESIGN-CARRIES: the shape of a solution (*how*, provisional)

p.MARK-THE-KIND-WHERE-AMBIGUITY-IS-POSSIBL: Mark the kind where ambiguity is possible — a one-line note under the heading is enough.

p.THE-CHEAPEST-FORM-IS-A-CONTRACT-ONLY-UNI: The cheapest form: put contracts in their own units and let the anchor name say so (`#verification.timeout`, not `#some-thoughts-on-timeouts`).

p.the-must-changes-rarely-the-why-does-not: The MUST changes rarely; the *why* evolves freely.

p.mixing-them-makes-every-edit-look-like-a: When both live in one paragraph, every rationale edit looks like a contract change, and every reader must re-verify code against a unit that did not actually move.

p.KEEP-THE-CONTRACT-SENTENCE-TIGHT: Keep the contract sentence tight and let the reasoning follow it in its own paragraph — or its own unit — so each can change without casting suspicion on the other.

p.IMPLEMENTATION-DETAIL-BELONGS-NEXT-TO-TH: Implementation detail belongs next to the code — doc comments, module docs — where it cannot drift from the code it describes.

p.A-SPEC-THAT-MIRRORS-CODE-IS-SHADOW-CODE: **A spec that mirrors code is shadow code and drift fuel**: two copies of the same *how*, one of which is compiled and one of which rots.

p.THE-REFACTOR-TEST: The test: if a refactor with identical behaviour would force a spec edit, the spec is standing too close to the code.

p.A-CONTRACT-UNIT-IMPLIES-ITS-OWN-VERIFICA: A contract unit should imply its own verification.

p.UNNAMEABLE-TEST-MEANS-DESIGN-NOT-CONTRAC: If you cannot name the test that would verify the statement, it is design, not contract — either sharpen it until a test is imaginable, or demote it and stop pretending it binds.

p.RECORD-THE-TEST-NAME-IN-THE-UNIT: Record the test name in the unit once it exists (`Test: …`); that line is half of the bidirectional graph described in the [protocol §graph](ADDRESSABLE-SPECS-PROTOCOL.xml#graph) — and where the project mechanizes that graph, the same half is authored as a tag on the test and rendered back at the unit instead, per that section.

deviations.title: Deviations are first-class

p.A-DEVIATION-IS-RECORDED-WHERE-IT-HAPPENS: When reality intentionally differs from the spec, the deviation is recorded at the point where it happens, with the reason — in the code near the deviating item, citing the violated anchor:

p.A-RECORDED-DEVIATION-AWAITS-REVIEW: A recorded deviation is a decision awaiting review.

p.AN-UNDOCUMENTED-DEVIATION-IS-A-DEFECT: An undocumented deviation discovered later is a defect — not because the code is wrong, but because the channel lied.

p.honest-deviations-keep-the-spec-authorit: Honest deviations are what keep the spec authoritative even while reality is ahead of it.

p.control-plane-tokens-are-a-per-session-t: Control-plane files are read every session; every token in them is a tax multiplied by the number of sessions the project will ever run.

td.ROW-BUDGET-BOOT-FILE-WHEN-OVER: cut; move detail into flow docs and cite

td.ROW-BUDGET-WAL-WHEN-OVER: collapse completed items to one line each

p.BUDGETS-GOVERN-AUTHORED-DOCUMENTS-ONLY: Every budget above governs an **authored** document. A **generated** artifact carries none — and the proof is in the last column: "cut", "collapse" and "split" are instructions to a writer, and a compiler's output has no writer to receive them. Its size is whatever the resolution graph says the session must have, so trimming it means changing what the project declared it needs, which is a different decision in a different file.

p.COMPILING-INTO-THE-LANE-IS-NOT-A-BUDGET-: It follows that a project which *compiles* its boot lane out of installed sources is not in breach when that lane grows, and "the artifact is over budget" is not a finding against it. The cost that stays real is the **session's** context — a live measurement about one run, not a static rule about one file, and this table is not where it is settled.

p.rule-of-thumb-500-tokens-is-a-page: Rule of thumb: 500 tokens is roughly 375 English words — one page.

p.THE-NUMBERS-ARE-BUDGETS-NOT-PHYSICS: The numbers are budgets, not physics; the direction of the pressure is what matters.

p.A-SPEC-PAST-ITS-BUDGET-IS-TWO-SPECS: A spec that keeps growing past its budget is not a big spec, it is two specs sharing a file.

p.split-triggers-lead: Split when any of these fires:

facts.SPLIT-WHEN-OVER-BUDGET: the document is over its size budget (§[budgets](#budgets));
facts.SPLIT-WHEN-A-UNIT-NEEDS-AND-ALSO: a unit needs "and also" — that is two units, and often two homes;
facts.SPLIT-WHEN-TWO-AUDIENCES-EMERGE: two audiences have emerged (contract readers vs tutorial readers);
facts.SPLIT-WHEN-ONE-SECTION-IS-CITED-FAR-MORE: one section is cited from outside far more than the rest — promote it to its own document so its URI shortens and its neighbours stop riding along into every context window.

p.SPLITTING-IS-CHEAP-IF-ANCHORS-SURVIVE: Splitting is cheap precisely because citations point at anchors, not page numbers — provided the anchors survive the move (§[anchor-stability](#anchor-stability)).

changelog.title: Changelog lines

p.EACH-SEMANTIC-CHANGE-APPENDS-A-DATED-LIN: Each semantic change to a document appends one dated line with the reason:

p.THE-CHANGELOG-IS-A-SIGNAL-NOT-HISTORY: The changelog is a signal, not history — history lives in git.

p.who-the-changelog-is-for: The changelog exists for the reader who last saw this file a week ago and needs the delta in five seconds, without running a diff.

anchor-stability.title: Anchor stability

p.A-CITED-ANCHOR-IS-A-PUBLIC-SYMBOL: An anchor that appears in code markers, commit bodies, other specs, or the WAL is a public symbol; renaming it is a breaking change that silently snaps every citation — the exact failure addressability exists to prevent.

facts.NEVER-RENAME-A-CITED-ANCHOR: Never rename a cited anchor. If the heading text must change, the `{#id}` stays.
facts.NEVER-REUSE-AN-ANCHOR-FOR-A-DIFFERENT-ME: Never reuse an anchor for a different meaning. An address that once meant one thing and now means another is worse than a dead link.
facts.RETIRE-WITH-A-TOMBSTONE-DO-NOT-DELETE: Retire with a tombstone, do not delete: `<!-- RETIRED: superseded by {#new-anchor} -->` under the old heading location.
facts.A-MOVED-UNIT-LEAVES-A-TOMBSTONE: Moving a unit to another document leaves a tombstone at the old address pointing to the new one.

p.delegate-the-audit-lead: Delegate the audit — it is mechanical and the agent is good at it:

anchor-stability.fence: Audit this repository for addressability: 1. List every spec heading that states a decision, constraint, or contract but carries no {#anchor}. 2. List every normative value that appears in more than one file. 3. List every spec:// citation (specs, code comments, commit log) that no longer resolves to an existing anchor. Report as three tables: location, problem, suggested fix. Do not edit anything yet.

facts.SUM-ONE-UNIT-ONE-DECISION: One unit, one decision; a unit makes sense alone, on one page.
facts.SUM-NORMATIVITY-IS-MARKED: Normativity is marked with RFC-2119 verbs — nobody guesses what binds.
facts.SUM-CONTRACT-AND-RATIONALE-ARE-SEPARATE: Contract and rationale are separate; the spec never restates *how*. A spec that mirrors code is shadow code.
facts.SUM-EVERY-CONTRACT-IMPLIES-A-TEST: Every contract implies a test; the unit names it, by a `Test:` line or by a rendered edge where the graph is mechanized.
facts.SUM-DEVIATIONS-ARE-RECORDED-WHERE-THEY-H: Deviations are recorded where they happen, with reasons; the undocumented one is the defect.
facts.SUM-THE-SIZE-BUDGETS: Budgets: boot ≤ 500 tokens, WAL ≤ 3000, module spec ≤ 5000 — split when over.
facts.SUM-THE-CHANGELOG-LINE: Changelog: one dated line per semantic change, with the reason.
facts.SUM-ANCHORS-ARE-IMMUTABLE: Anchors are immutable once cited; retirement is a tombstone, never a deletion or a silent rename.
